newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX natgas still mixed, cash off slightly.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX natgas still mixed, cash off slightly.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained narrowly mixed late Friday in moderate trade, with September lightly pressured by some pre-weekend profit taking in the face of a softer physical market.
At 1435 EDT, September was still down 0.3 cent at $2.425 per million British thermal units, while October was 0.3 cent higher at $2.46. Most others were steady to up three cents.

"I thought we'd break down more today after yesterday's late selloff, but September rebounded immediately when they couldn't break it below $2.40," said one New York-based futures trader, noting cash was down slightly for the weekend but still above the screen and talk of a fairly tight supply/demand balance was keeping the bears at bay.

Technical traders still pegged September resistance at yesterday's high of $2.55 and then at the contract high and double top at $2.605. Further selling was likely at the $2.64-2.655 spot continuation chart gap from late January. Support was seen at $2.395, $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely in the $2.25-2.27 area.
After a brief weekend warmup in the Midwest and Northeast, temperatures next week in most regions are expected to return to seasonal to slightly-below seasonal levels.

In the cash Friday, Gulf Coast weekend prices slipped slightly to about the $2.50 level. Midcon pipes were steady to modestly lower in the low-$2.40s. New York city gate gas was little changed in the mid-$2.70s.
NYMEX volume figures were unavailable. Hub open interest on August 14 fell 785 contracts to 222,363.
On KCBT, September climbed one cent to $2.35, while deferreds were steady to a half cent higher. The East/West spread narrowed 1.3 cents to 7.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
